_doc: Coding-agent CLIs the Blurt app can hand a recording to, headless. Read by agents.py and by the macOS app (BlurtRecorder: Agents.swift; a copy is bundled into Blurt.app/Contents/Resources). Order of `agents` = default fallback order; the user's order is config record.agents. A custom agent can be added in config record.agent_defs with the same fields. status: how to tell whether it is logged in without spending tokens — `args` run with a 15 s timeout, then: json_key (a bool in the first JSON object of the output) > creds_json ({path, keys}: the file exists and every key is empty → logged out) > provider_toml ({path, key, profile, profiles, except}: the TOML config selects a model provider not in `except` — at the top, or in the [<profiles>.<name>] its top-level `profile` names — → configured: codex pointed at another provider by cc-switch & co. has no ChatGPT login and needs none; it also hides models.cache, OpenAI's list) > logged_out (substrings) > ok_if (substrings, exit 0) > configured_if (regex: has credentials, can't verify them) > env_any / files_any (credentials in env / on disk) > otherwise ('logged_out' | 'unknown'). run: the headless command, {prompt} = the task text — only ever unattended (organising a recording or a batch of cards, AI fill-in, drafts) on text taken from the user's screen and voice, so it gets the least privilege that still lets it file items. Its cwd is the session folder (AI fill-in: a scratch folder), never the project; it reads the project's code but writes nothing there. No full-access / yolo modes. claude / gemini: file edits only inside cwd (acceptEdits / auto_edit) and shell commands only the skill scripts an organizing run uses, each pinned to its absolute path ({scripts} = the skill's scripts folder; the prompt names the same path) — no other command, no other script. codex: its workspace-write sandbox, writable = cwd + {writable} (one `--add-dir` each: the inbox store, every project's .blurt store, and a uv cache of its own — env UV_CACHE_DIR, BLURT_NO_INDEX; agents.py sandbox_env); never $BLURT_HOME (config.json, the jobs, index.db) nor the shared uv cache, so nothing it writes runs outside the sandbox later; network stays on because uv resolves the scripts' dependencies. grok: --permission-mode dontAsk (a call no rule allows is refused, never asked: nobody is there to answer), file edits only inside cwd (Edit(./**)) and the same skill scripts, each pinned to its absolute path; --disable-web-search because grok runs web search and fetch without asking in every mode, dontAsk included (a prompt injected through the screen could otherwise send what it reads out in a query), and --no-auto-update; its status is `grok models` (prints "You are logged in…", no tokens spent; it needs the network, so when it fails without saying either way, auth.json on disk counts as configured). A project's .blurt/config.json can't define agents (agents.py config). kimi / opencode: their own -p / run defaults (flags not verified). verified: 'run' = a real headless run was checked, 'cli' = flags checked with --help only, 'docs' = from the CLI's documentation. WP2 fields (agents.py detect / command / install): version = args printing the version; events = args appended to run for machine-readable progress + its format; headless: false = never run unattended (skip it in the auto chain: Connect only); app = {macos | windows | linux: path, or a list of paths tried in order} for app-only agents (none for this OS: listed as not installed); skill_dir = where the blurt skill is linked (a symlink; on Windows a directory junction, which needs no Developer Mode, else a copy); mcp = {args (+check: args that exit 0 when already added; current: values the check's output must name — else the entry is stale and written again, after `remove` for a CLI that won't add over it; approve: {path, server, tools} = Codex's per-tool approval_mode = "approve" for the reporting tools only, written to its config.toml after the server is registered, so an unattended run with approval never can still report back — nothing that takes a key) | json: {path, key, value} merged into a config file}, {mcp_server} = absolute path of mcp_server.py, {uv} = uv's absolute path, used by every entry: the agent starts the server itself, desktop apps (Cursor, WorkBuddy) without the login shell's PATH, and on Windows / Linux the app's uv lives in $BLURT_HOME/bin, on no one else's PATH. codebuddy / workbuddy / cursor: connect only (skill + MCP; headless: false), paths from their documentation (WorkBuddy: the paths its app reads, ~/.workbuddy/skills and ~/.workbuddy/mcp.json); cursor links into ~/.agents/skills, which Cursor reads like ~/.claude/skills. Paths take ~ and ${VAR:-default}. headless_mcp = args `agents.py command … headless` adds so the run can use the blurt MCP server with no prompts (codex: the whole server via -c, since -c on an unregistered server breaks codex, plus approve mode and the BLURT_* env it forwards); {mcp_server_json} / {uv_json} = those paths as JSON/TOML strings. Processing (v0.7): models = where the agent's models are listed ({list: [{id, name, cheap}]} | {cache: the CLI's own model cache, format ('codex': a list of {slug, priority, visibility}; 'grok': a map of id → {info: {name, description, hidden}}, never a cheap one — its fast model costs more), config: its config file for the current default, config_key: that setting's TOML key (default `model`; dotted = in a table, grok's models.default)}); model_args = how a model / an effort level is passed ({model}, {effort}); processing = the defaults for unattended organising runs, per kind: recording (organizing a recording: the CLI's own model at low effort) and cards (snap / voice-note batches, AI fill-in, small runs: the cheapest model) — each {model: id | 'cheapest' (the cache's or list's cheap model) | 'default' (the CLI's own setting), effort: level | 'default'}; the v0.8 shape {model, effort} still means both. Overridden per agent and kind by config record.agent_processing.<id>.<kind> (Settings → Agents); usage = how a run reports the tokens it used (args added to the processing run + format | pattern with the number in group 1). Finding and connecting (v1.0.26, docs/design/agent-setup.md §8; agents.py detect): home = the agent's own config folder (a path or a list; ~ and ${VAR:-default}) — it existing is the signal that a skill / MCP config written there will be read, and Connect writes there even when nothing was found (Connect anyway); app = {macos: bundle ids, windows: program stems (lowercase, no .exe), linux: .desktop ids} found without starting anything (LaunchServices / Info.plist, the Uninstall keys + App Paths + Start Menu shortcuts + Scoop / WinGet links, XDG / Flatpak / Snap .desktop files), a path is still taken as a fallback; found = home exists or app found (cached 10 min). mcp_clients = the clientInfo.name values the agent's MCP client sends (the server notes them in $BLURT_HOME/run/mcp-clients.json: connected); edition = which edition, for two entries of one product (WorkBuddy 国内版 / WorkBuddy AI 国际版); site = its download page; after = what to do in the agent after Connect; connect: false = not listed for Connect (a card-drag target only). drop = composer | terminal (or {os: …}): a card dragged into the app is the picture's path and its note (composer: one line per card, terminal: one line) — the one list CardDropTarget.swift and card_drop.rs read, with record.agent_defs (the user's own) and record.agent_drop.<id> = false (switched off). verified / app_verified / skill_verified: run | cli | docs | local (seen on a real install) | unverified (a best guess: a user who finds it wrong uses Other Agent…).
